newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese president said to threaten resignation.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese president said to threaten resignation.

text.p: Lebanon's President Elias Hrawi was reported on Tuesday to be threatening to resign because of an apparent government decision to postpone the first local elections in 34 years.
Newspapers said Hrawi, a 70-year-old Maronite Christian, told visitors on Monday he would resign if the municipal council and mayoral elections were not held this summer as scheduled.
"I want the elections held at all costs. It's either elections or I go home. There is no other alternative," the leftist Beirut daily as-Safir and the conservative an-Nahar quoted Hrawi as saying.

Lebanon's first local elections since 1963 are scheduled for June 1 and 8, but doubts that they will be held arose when the government last week withdrew from parliament a bill to amend the election law.
Lebanon's political elite are widely considered to feel uneasy about the vote, fearing the results could weaken their grip on power.
This is partly because all Christian opposition groups, including those which have boycotted national elections since the 1975-90 civil war, have decided to take part.
According to sources close to Hrawi, he believes that postponing the polls would demoralise Lebanese voters and damage the state's credibility.
It was believed to be the first time Hrawi had threatened to quit, even indirectly, since he took office in November 1989 before the end of the civil war.

Parliament Speaker Berri was quoted on Tuesday as saying the withdrawal of the election bill meant postponement of the polls, even though Hrawi and billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri set up a ministerial committee on Sunday to draft new amendments within 15 days.
"I think we will end up having municipalities and mayors appointed rather than elected," an-Nahar quoted Berri as saying.
Newspapers said Hrawi was angry with Hariri and Berri for concocting an "under-the-table" accord to have the election bill withdrawn from parliament.
Parliamentary deputy Roucheid el-Khazen told the French-language daily L'Orient-Le Jour Hrawi felt betrayed.
He considered the withdrawal of the bill unconstitutional because government drafts could be withdrawn from parliament only by a joint decision of the president and prime minister, Khazen added.
Neither Berri nor Hariri has given any reason for wanting to delay the polls. They criticised the draft amendments and said changes proposed by deputies had to be discussed by the government.
